title: Co-Investigating with a First Love
notes: No human victim -- this is a vigilante vandalism/hit-and-run case (case_type: vandalism), not a murder, so `label.murderer_id` here names the vandal/culprit rather than a killer, kept under that key name only for schema consistency with the other cases. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. Recurring fully-generic detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro, Ran, Ai Haibara, Agasa, Detective Boys, Inspector Megure, Takagi) omitted by convention, but Chiba, Naeko Mi'ike, and Yumi Miyamoto are included despite also being recurring franchise characters because they carry the episode's actual B-plot (Chiba's own car is victim #4 of the serial vandal, and the matchmaking subplot runs through nearly every scene). The old lower-fidelity cases/ file got the core whodunit right (Tokuko Shigei, parking lot, spray-paint object) but was missing almost everything else that gives the case its shape: the backstory victim (her son, killed by a driver whose rear-view was blocked by beach gear), the unnamed driver responsible, the two forensic clues that actually crack the case (a child-car-seat sunburn mark on her own back seat, and lipstick from the airbag impact hidden under matching spray paint on her own windscreen), the trap car (Sato Miwako's FD, decorated as bait), and the full set of targeted vehicles and why each was or wasn't chosen (every target had an obstructed rear window; Meiwa's superficially similar car was spared because its spoiler sat high enough not to block the view).

clues.desc: Sunburn/tan-line pattern on the back seat of Shigei's own car matches a child car seat, contradicting her claim of having no kids or toys and revealing the son she never mentioned.

Lipstick transferred to the deployed airbag during the collision was hidden under fresh spray paint matching the "Die!" message, proving the message on her own windscreen was self-applied, not the work of an outside vandal.

Every targeted car (itasha decal, golf bags, low spoiler, toy figures) had its rear window obstructed, while Meiwa's similarly flashy car -- high spoiler, clear rear window -- was left alone, showing the vandal selects by blocked visibility, not by owner type.
